patterns_found.visual_evidence: The mobile sketch shows a compact top navigation/header treatment rather than a full horizontal nav, implying a collapsed mobile menu trigger is needed to reveal navigation options.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: A mobile nav toggle should open and close the hidden navigation panel, likely overlaying or pushing content below the header.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The hamburger icon itself is not clearly drawn in the sketch, so the collapsed-menu behavior is inferred from the simplified mobile header and the desktop comparison.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The desktop sketch includes a horizontal navigation bar with multiple grouped nav items and circular markers/caret-like indicators beside some items, implying submenu triggers.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Desktop nav items with indicators should reveal submenu panels on click or hover; submenus should dismiss on outside click and support keyboard access.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not make clear whether submenus open on hover or click, nor how many levels of nesting exist.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: Both sketches depict a long article-like page with substantial vertical scrolling; the reference context also suggests a back-to-top affordance for long content.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: A back-to-top control should appear after the user scrolls down and smoothly return focus/scroll position to the top when activated.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The exact placement and visibility threshold are not explicit in the sketches.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The desktop sketch emphasizes a persistent horizontal navigation bar near the top spanning the page width, which strongly suggests it should remain accessible while scrolling through long content.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: The top navigation may stay fixed or become fixed after scrolling past the header so section/site navigation remains available on long pages.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch alone does not explicitly show a fixed state; this is inferred from the long-scroll layout and prominent nav bar.

sketch_notes: The sketches imply a mostly content-driven page with relatively light JavaScript needs centered on navigation and long-scroll assistance rather than forms or dynamic modules. The main cross-viewport difference is navigation behavior: mobile likely collapses into a toggleable menu, while desktop exposes a horizontal nav with possible dropdowns and perhaps sticky behavior. The rest of the page appears largely static article content with optional back-to-top support due to the page length.
